text.content:
2047: the ordinances, the sweeps, and the street map redrawn.

When: Late August to September 2047
Where: The Old Combat Zone, Little China, Little Europe, Heywood, Watson
Who was involved: The City Council, a rogue Militech cell, the NCPD and MaxTac, and nearly every gang in the city
What it changed: Dozens of small gangs died; the survivors got big. The NCPD became the city's one badge

The First Ordinance

In late August 2047 rogue Militech hands on the Council pushed through Ordinance 47-8, the "Clean Streets Ordinance", now called the first Purge Ordinance. Gang association became a felony: wearing colors, paying dues or "acting in concert" with a listed gang. The List attached to it named most of the small gangs in the city, but not the big ones. The NCPD ran the sweeps with unbadged "temporary security contractors" everyone knew were Militech, through the Old Combat Zone and the small-gang turf of Little China and Little Europe, and most of the city looked away.

The Second Ordinance

Thirty-six hours after the lights came back on Static Night, the Council's Militech friends gave the city a story: gang netrunners had nearly crashed the city. An emergency session passed Ordinance 47-9, the Public Order Restoration Ordinance, the second Purge Ordinance, and the one people mean by "the Purge". The List grew to name almost every gang. The Militech contractors were sent home, and a fat new city contract went to MaxTac instead. Sweeps doubled into block-by-block occupation, and detention camps went up in the old Reclamation Zone, holding people without charge for up to ninety days, and some longer.

The Purge-Riot

On the fourth night of raids the city fought back. The Purge-Riot burned for four nights across Heywood, Watson and Little Europe, as gangers, kids and workers set fire to precinct houses and armored trucks and the occupation answered with military rounds. The official dead number 341. Nobody on the badge side wanted to count the rest.

Who Died, Who Didn't

  • Wiped out: the Bozos, Piranhas, Eurotrashers, Philharmonic Vampyres, Inquisitors, Generation Red, Rat Kings, Zoners, Shroomers, Kill Krashers, Lightning Cats, Albino Alligators, Toecutters, Wild Things, Dragula Racers, the Enhanced, the Julliard Guild, the Undertow, the G3, and the old Voodoo Boys of Baron D.
  • Absorbed by Maelstrom: the Iron Sights and the Red Chrome Legion.
  • Absorbed by the Tyger Claws: the Mudang Gumi, the Gold Dragons' remnants, and every yakuza clan and East Asian syndicate that wanted to keep breathing, except the Usagi.
  • Driven underground: the cartels and the Steel Vaqueros, who came back as the Valentinos after Moto Cielo.
  • Survived under a wing: the DeadWoods, the Princesses of Justice, the Muses, the Dirty Hippies, Fixie's Couriers and the Usagi.
  • Untouched: the Old Three, Maelstrom, the Tyger Claws and 6th Street, none of them on the List. The Claws had the Sphere and Arasaka's old friends; 6th Street had veterans in every precinct and Militech's sympathy; Maelstrom had somebody, and nobody knows who.

Aftermath

Max Hammerman folded MaxTac back into the NCPD, and the NCPD became the city's one legal enforcement agency; the private district providers lost their contracts over the following years. Neither Ordinance has been repealed: gang association is still a felony on paper, rarely charged and always threatened. Ziggurat lost the CitiNet in 2049 and died in 2051. Every big gang in 2070 is an Old Three survivor or New Blood from after the Red, and the booster crews that lasted did it by standing behind one of them.

Night City 2070 (The Unification Era), ch.02
